test: Compute on-hand qty per SKU-branch at day 2520 as the running sum of WMS qty_delta, value at erp_products.unit_cost. Classify pairs as dead (no sale movement in days 2269-2520) and excess (on hand > 2x trailing-252-day sales qty). Compare shares of total value to the 10% threshold. Then break down by category, discontinued flag, opening-balance presence, branch; track the same measure at each year-end (days 252, 504, ... 2520) for persistence; check receipts in the last year into dead/excess pairs; compare stock value to annual COGS at standard cost.
support: Dead + excess share >10% of on-hand value, persisting across year-ends at the same pairs, receipts still arriving into excess pairs, concentrated in discontinued SKUs, not explained by missing opening balances or seasonality.
weaken: Dead share small (<10%) and excess explained by seasonal equipment or by pairs with no opening balance (balances misstated); stock value only ~2-3 months of COGS; dead/excess pairs rotate year to year rather than persisting.
expect: Dead stock ~8% of value (2.6M of 32.9M) alone just under 10%, but excess >2 years ~19% so the union exceeds 10%. Moderately confident the hypothesis holds on the stated test, but I suspect much of it is a simulation artefact: constant reorder logic receiving into pairs whose demand has moved (discontinued SKUs still selling). Expect overall stock-to-COGS to be low (a few months), so the business-level overstock is moderate. Confidence ~60% that the finding stands as a material, persistent excess.
